text.zh: 他来自加勒比海。商行的账本教会他计算，海上的风暴教会他：一个人的处境，可能在一夜之间被改写。
text.en: He came from the Caribbean. A merchant's ledgers taught him to reckon; storms at sea taught him that a life could be rewritten overnight.

text.zh: 他把所见写成文字。有人读了那篇文章，开始相信，这个年轻人应该得到继续求学的机会。
text.en: He put what he had seen into words. People read them and began to believe this young man deserved the chance to continue his education.

text.zh: 我带不走那座岛。但我能带走纸上的每一个字。纽约有学校，有印刷机，也有人愿意争论未来。我要在那里找到我的位置。
text.en: I cannot take the island with me. But I can carry every word on the page. New York has schools, printing presses, and people willing to argue about the future. I will find my place there.

text.zh: 港口的消息！英军动向、商船货价，还有一整版互相反驳的文章。先生，你想知道发生了什么，还是想让别人知道你是谁？
text.en: News from the harbor! British troop movements, cargo prices, and a whole page of writers contradicting each other. Sir, do you want to know what is happening, or let people know who you are?

text.zh: 先给我一份。只有知道这座城在为什么争吵，我的文字才不会只是对着自己说话。
text.en: Give me a copy first. Until I know what this city is arguing about, my writing will only be a conversation with myself.

text.zh: 驻军越来越多。有人说军队保护生意，可我只想知道：他们保护的是谁作决定的权利？
text.en: More troops arrive every day. They say the army protects trade. But whose right to decide are they protecting?

text.zh: 没有王室和海军，这座港口靠什么维持秩序？你们把眼前的生计，押给一个还不存在的国家。
text.en: Without the Crown and its navy, what keeps order in this port? You would stake today's livelihood on a country that does not yet exist.

text.zh: 这两个人都害怕失去手里的生活。但他们还没问过，谁有资格替另一方下注。
text.en: Both are afraid of losing the lives they have. Neither has asked who has the right to make that wager for the other.

text.zh: 你听了很久。亚历山大·汉密尔顿，对吗？我读过你的文字。
text.en: You have been listening for a while. Alexander Hamilton, isn't it? I have read your work.

text.zh: 那就省了介绍。你也听见了——他们谈论自由的时候，仿佛每个人说的是不同的东西。
text.en: Then we can skip the introductions. You heard them too: when they speak of freedom, they seem to mean entirely different things.

text.zh: 先弄清楚谁在听，再决定说多少。局势会变；公开说过的话，会留下来。
text.en: Learn who is listening before you decide how much to say. Circumstances change. Words spoken in public remain.

text.zh: 先观察，弄清各方的立场。
text.en: Observe first and understand where each side stands.

text.zh: 很好。耐心也能是一种行动。我们去酒馆，那里比街头容易听见真话。
text.en: Good. Patience can be a form of action. Come to the tavern. It is easier to hear people speak plainly there.

text.zh: 那你呢？你自己相信什么？
text.en: And you? What do you believe?

text.zh: 我相信，作决定之前应该把人看清楚。你这个问题，让我更想认识你了。走吧。
text.en: I believe in knowing people before making decisions. That question makes me more interested in knowing you. Come along.

text.zh: 我支持革命。现在就可以写下我的名字。
text.en: I support the revolution. You can put my name to it now.

text.zh: 我听见了。整条街也听见了。希望你准备好了，为这么响亮的名字负责。
text.en: I heard you. So did the whole street. I hope you are ready to answer for a name spoken that loudly.

text.zh: 我们把自由写得那么大，却总把某些人留在句子外面。一个仍允许奴役的国家，准备怎样解释自己的自由？
text.en: We write freedom in such large letters, yet always leave certain people outside the sentence. How will a country that still permits slavery explain its freedom?

text.zh: 你要的答案，恐怕会让这张桌子安静下来。
text.en: The answer you want may bring this table to a silence.

text.zh: 那就让它安静。你认为现在最重要的是什么？
text.en: Then let it fall silent. What do you think matters most right now?

text.zh: 先维持秩序，让人们活过这场战争。
text.en: Preserve order so people survive the war.

text.zh: 活下来当然重要。可有些人一直在等“以后”，我们不能再轻易替他们说这个词。
text.en: Surviving matters, of course. But some people have always been told to wait until later. We cannot keep saying that on their behalf.

text.zh: 谁来作决定，谁又有权提出反对？
text.en: Who gets to decide, and who has the right to object?

text.zh: 那么，记得把被排除的人也算进去。换一个掌权的人，还不够。
text.en: Then remember to include those who have been excluded. Replacing the people in power is not enough.

text.zh: 自由的承诺，应当包含被奴役的人。
text.en: The promise of freedom must include enslaved people.

text.zh: 我愿意和这样的人并肩。但当这个承诺开始让盟友不舒服时，你还得说下去。
text.en: I would stand beside someone who believes that. But when that promise begins to trouble our allies, you must keep saying it.

text.zh: 你沉默了一会儿。没关系，先听听其他人的想法；这张桌子还会留一个位置。
text.en: You fall silent for a moment. That's all right. Listen to the others first; there will still be a place for you at this table.

text.zh: 我横渡大西洋，不是为了旁观。可勇气不能替士兵装满口粮。面对更强的军队，你准备把力气用在哪里？
text.en: I did not cross the Atlantic to watch. But courage cannot fill a soldier's ration bag. Against a stronger army, where will you put your effort?

text.zh: 每一条路都要付代价。区别在于，我们愿不愿意自己选择。
text.en: Every path has a price. The difference is whether we are willing to choose for ourselves.

text.zh: 保持谈判，为居民争取喘息。
text.en: Keep negotiating to give civilians room to breathe.

text.zh: 可以。但谈判桌也需要有人在外面守着。别把喘息误当成终点。
text.en: Perhaps. But someone must stand guard outside the negotiating room. Do not mistake a breath of air for the end of the journey.

text.zh: 建立联盟，把孤军变成共同事业。
text.en: Build alliances and turn an isolated struggle into a shared cause.

text.zh: 那你得学会听见盟友的需要。共同事业，不能只有一个人的声音。
text.en: Then you must learn to hear what your allies need. A shared cause cannot speak in only one person's voice.

text.zh: 公开争取独立，不再等待许可。
text.en: Demand independence openly, without waiting for permission.

text.zh: 够直接。我喜欢。但说完这句话，下一步就该准备行军了。
text.en: Direct enough. I like it. But after those words, the next step is preparing to march.

text.zh: 你沉默了一会儿。没关系，先听听其他人的想法；这张桌子还会留一个位置。
text.en: You fall silent for a moment. That's all right. Listen to the others first; there will still be a place for you at this table.

text.zh: 大道理我听够了。明早有十个人愿意帮忙，一家印刷铺肯赊账，还有一辆空车。汉密尔顿，你怎么用？
text.en: I've heard enough grand ideas. Tomorrow, ten people will help, a printer will extend credit, and there's an empty wagon. Hamilton, how will you use them?

text.zh: 你给我的不是十个人，是十个人各自认识的那条街。
text.en: You have given me more than ten people. You have given me every street they know.

text.zh: 印一份清楚的传单，让每条街接着讨论。
text.en: Print a clear pamphlet to keep the conversation going in every street.

text.zh: 行。少写几个漂亮词，多写几句他们能讲给邻居听的话。
text.en: Good. Fewer elegant phrases, more lines they can repeat to their neighbors.

text.zh: 先送补给，让愿意加入的人吃上饭。
text.en: Deliver supplies first so people willing to join us can eat.

text.zh: 车我来找。愿意做这种不显眼的事，才有人下次还来找你。
text.en: I'll find the wagon. Be willing to do the work no one notices, and people will come to you again.

text.zh: 召集公开集会，今天就让更多人听见。
text.en: Call a public meeting and make more people hear us today.

text.zh: 场地可以有。巡逻队一来，你可不能只顾着自己的演说。
text.en: We can find a place. But when the patrol arrives, you cannot think only of your speech.

text.zh: 你沉默了一会儿。没关系，先听听其他人的想法；这张桌子还会留一个位置。
text.en: You fall silent for a moment. That's all right. Listen to the others first; there will still be a place for you at this table.

text.zh: 脱离英国之后，商船由谁护送，货物卖给谁？你们用自由作保证，却要每一个家庭拿生计来冒险。
text.en: Once you break from Britain, who escorts the ships, and who buys the cargo? You offer freedom as a guarantee, but ask every family to risk its livelihood.

text.zh: 这也是我想问的。没有明天的面包，今天的口号有什么用？
text.en: That is what I want to know. Without tomorrow's bread, what good are today's slogans?

text.zh: 他们在等你的回答。把问题听完。
text.en: They are waiting for your answer. Hear the whole question.

text.zh: 脱离英国之后，商船由谁护送，货物卖给谁？你们让每个家庭用明天的面包支付自由。
text.en: After leaving Britain, who will escort the ships and buy the cargo? You ask each family to pay for freedom with tomorrow's bread.

text.zh: 把税负与贸易限制也算进去。
text.en: Count taxes and trade restrictions too.

text.zh: 承担代价的人应有决定权。
text.en: Those who pay should have a say.

text.zh: 你为何只计算改变的代价？
text.en: Why count only the costs of change?

text.zh: 让码头的人说说他们的账本。
text.en: Let the dockworkers open their ledgers.

text.zh: 帝国的议会已经替各地考虑过了。若每座港口都要求自己决定，法律还剩下什么？
text.en: Parliament has already considered every region. If each port insists on deciding for itself, what is left of the law?

text.zh: 把殖民地的代表席位列出来。
text.en: List the colonies' seats in Parliament.

text.zh: 服从法律，也应参与制定。
text.en: Those who obey laws should help make them.

text.zh: 考虑过，不等于听过我们的声音。
text.en: Considering us is not the same as hearing us.

text.zh: 谁愿意让别人决定自己的税？
text.en: Who wants others to decide their taxes?

text.zh: 倡议革命的人只会写文章。等粮食短缺，他们会让穷人承担后果。
text.en: The advocates of revolution only write essays. When food runs short, they will leave the poor to bear the consequences.

text.zh: 补给方案与责任人必须公开。
text.en: Publish the supply plan and those responsible.

text.zh: 自由不能只属于有余粮的人。
text.en: Freedom cannot belong only to the well-fed.

text.zh: 你也没给穷人留下别的出路。
text.en: You have offered the poor no other path.

text.zh: 请工人和店主自己提出条件。
text.en: Let workers and shopkeepers name their terms.

text.zh: 驻军只为保护秩序。既然你们没有做错什么，为何害怕更多巡逻？
text.en: The garrison is only here to keep order. If you have done nothing wrong, why fear more patrols?

text.zh: 检查驻军的权限与费用。
text.en: Examine the garrison's powers and costs.

text.zh: 权力仍需得到被治理者同意。
text.en: Power still needs the consent of the governed.

text.zh: 要求解释，何时成了认错？
text.en: Since when is asking for an explanation a confession?

text.zh: 请居民讲讲巡逻带来的变化。
text.en: Let residents describe what patrols have changed.

text.zh: 帝国拥有舰队和资金。你们连统一的军需账册都没有，却要把大家带进战争。
text.en: The empire has fleets and money. You do not even have a common supply ledger, yet you would lead everyone into war.

text.zh: 统一账册，逐项落实补给。
text.en: Unify the ledgers and secure supplies item by item.

text.zh: 危险不能取消选择的权利。
text.en: Danger does not erase the right to choose.

text.zh: 你的胜算只是让我们永远服从。
text.en: Your only plan is that we obey forever.

text.zh: 把愿意承担的工作写在这里。
text.en: Write down the work you are willing to do.

text.zh: 即使赢了，谁能保证新掌权的人更好？你们只是把一种不确定换成另一种。
text.en: Even if you win, who guarantees the new rulers will be better? You are exchanging one uncertainty for another.

text.zh: 将任期与问责写进制度。
text.en: Put terms of office and accountability into law.

text.zh: 让人民保留更换掌权者的权利。
text.en: Keep the people's right to replace their rulers.

text.zh: 没有保证，不等于现状无需改变。
text.en: No guarantee does not mean no need for change.

text.zh: 把你们不愿再接受的事说出来。
text.en: Tell us what you will no longer accept.

text.zh: 我看过你的文章。你能把事情写清楚。但军中需要的，还有把事情做完。
text.en: I have read your essays. You make matters clear. But an army also needs people who finish the work.

text.zh: 我希望带兵。我的能力不该只留在信纸上。
text.en: I want to lead troops. My ability should not stay on the page.

text.zh: 军令、情报、补给。写错一个地点，也会有人付出代价。我需要副官。你愿意从这里开始吗？
text.en: Orders, intelligence, supplies. A wrong place name can cost lives. I need an aide. Are you willing to begin here?

text.zh: 你的文章已经传进军营。我也听说了街上的争论。让别人注意你，你很擅长；让别人依靠你，是另一回事。
text.en: Your essays have reached camp. So has news of the argument in the street. You are good at drawing attention. Making yourself dependable is another matter.

text.zh: 那么给我一支队伍。我愿意用行动证明。
text.en: Then give me a company. I am willing to prove myself through action.

text.zh: 先做我的副官。军令、情报和补给，也决定着一支队伍能不能回来。你愿意承担吗？
text.en: Serve as my aide first. Orders, intelligence, and supplies also decide whether a company comes home. Will you take that responsibility?

text.zh: 接受副官职位，先完成眼前的责任。
text.en: Accept the post and fulfill the responsibility at hand.

text.zh: 很好。今晚有几封信，不能等到明天。
text.en: Good. Several letters tonight cannot wait until tomorrow.

text.zh: 接受，同时明确争取未来的指挥机会。
text.en: Accept, while making clear that you want a future command.

text.zh: 我听清了你的要求。你也要听清我的：用现在的职责，证明我能交给你下一份职责。
text.en: I have heard your request. Hear mine as well: prove through your present duties that I can trust you with the next ones.

text.zh: 我属于战场，应当立刻得到指挥权。
text.en: I belong on the battlefield and should be given command now.

text.zh: 这里没有人只凭“应当”获得命令权。今晚你仍然从这些军令开始。
text.en: No one here receives command merely because he thinks he should. Tonight, you will still begin with these dispatches.

text.zh: 北线的部队需要补给。驻地、出发时间、目的地都在这些报告里。给军需官一份能够执行的命令。
text.en: The northern troops need supplies. Their camp, the departure time, and the destination are in these reports. Give the quartermaster an order he can carry out.

text.zh: 一页纸。不能让收信人猜测，也不能让他在一段漂亮文字里寻找自己的任务。
text.en: One page. The reader must not have to guess, or search through fine prose to find his task.

text.zh: 运送面粉二十桶、药品两箱。
text.en: Deliver twenty barrels of flour and two crates of medicine.

text.zh: 接收地点为北线河岸营地。
text.en: The receiving point is the northern riverside camp.

text.zh: 明日拂晓前必须抵达。
text.en: Arrive before dawn tomorrow.

text.zh: 由军需官率一队士兵护送车队。
text.en: The quartermaster leads a squad escorting the wagons.

text.zh: 首先解除北线断粮的危险。
text.en: First, prevent the northern troops from running out of food.

text.zh: 旧石桥受损，东岸渡口仍可通行。
text.en: The old stone bridge is damaged; the eastern ferry still operates.

text.zh: 医官带担架队经渡口护送伤员。
text.en: The surgeon leads the stretcher party across the ferry.

text.zh: 优先将重伤员转移到后方医院。
text.en: Move the seriously wounded to the rear hospital first.

text.zh: 携带绷带、饮水与两辆空车。
text.en: Bring bandages, water, and two empty wagons.

text.zh: 今晚日落前完成转移。
text.en: Complete the transfer before sunset today.

text.zh: 后日清晨六时前完成准备。
text.en: Finish preparations by six the morning after tomorrow.

text.zh: 首要任务是保障各队准时集结。
text.en: The first priority is to have every squad muster on time.

text.zh: 集结地在磨坊以南的空地。
text.en: The muster point is the clearing south of the mill.

text.zh: 每队领取两日口粮并核对弹药。
text.en: Each squad collects two days of rations and checks its ammunition.

text.zh: 传令兵通知各队队长清点人数。
text.en: A messenger tells each squad leader to count their men.

text.zh: 1781 年，法美联军围困约克镇。数年的行军、军令与争执，终于把汉密尔顿带到一座英军堡垒前。
text.en: In 1781, French and American forces surrounded Yorktown. Years of marches, dispatches, and disputes brought Hamilton to the foot of a British redoubt.

text.zh: 你得到这次指挥机会。我要看到的，是一个能对整支队伍负责的军官。严格执行计划，别把它变成你一个人的证明。
text.en: You have this command. What I expect is an officer responsible for his whole company. Follow the plan. Do not turn it into a private test of your worth.

text.zh: 我明白。等了这么久，我不能只想着自己如何被看见。
text.en: I understand. After waiting so long, I cannot think only of how I will be seen.

text.zh: 1781 年，法美联军围困约克镇。数年的行军与军令，把汉密尔顿带到一座英军堡垒前。
text.en: In 1781, French and American forces surrounded Yorktown. Years of marches and dispatches brought Hamilton to the foot of a British redoubt.

text.zh: 你证明了自己能承担责任。这支队伍交给你。按计划行动；现场需要判断时，我相信你知道命令背后的目的。
text.en: You have proved you can carry responsibility. These troops are yours. Follow the plan; when judgment is needed, I trust you to understand the purpose behind the order.

text.zh: 这一次，纸上的名字会和我一起向前。我会记住，他们要跟随的不是一句漂亮的话。
text.en: This time, the names on the page will move forward beside me. I will remember that they need more than a fine sentence to follow.

text.zh: 核对各队的职责，等共同信号再推进。
text.en: Confirm each squad's role and wait for the common signal.

text.zh: 每一队都要知道身旁的人在哪里。听到信号，一起前进。
text.en: Every squad must know where the others are. When the signal comes, we move together.

text.zh: 我走在最前面，你们跟紧。
text.en: I will lead from the front. Stay close.

text.zh: 我会先走出去。但看清信号，别因为跟随我而忘了自己的位置。
text.en: I will step out first. But watch the signal. Do not lose your own position by following mine.

text.zh: 说明共同目标，让每个人知道为何出发。
text.en: Explain the shared objective so everyone knows why we are going.

text.zh: 我们要打开围城的一道缺口。记住身边的人，记住回来的路。现在，各就各位。
text.en: We are opening a breach in the siege. Remember the person beside you, and remember the way back. Now, take your positions.

text.zh: 推进
text.en: ADVANCE · Move forward

text.zh: 稳住阵形
text.en: HOLD · Steady the formation

text.zh: 左翼包抄
text.en: LEFT FLANK · Circle left

text.zh: 推进
text.en: ADVANCE · Move forward

text.zh: 右翼支援
text.en: RIGHT FLANK · Support the right

text.zh: 等待友军
text.en: HOLD · Wait for allied troops

text.zh: 侧翼接应
text.en: LEFT FLANK · Support the flank

text.zh: 越过土垒
text.en: ADVANCE · Cross the earthworks

text.zh: 保持联系
text.en: RIGHT FLANK · Maintain contact

text.zh: 重新集结
text.en: HOLD · Regroup

text.zh: 进入堡垒
text.en: ADVANCE · Enter the redoubt

text.zh: 守住阵地
text.en: HOLD · Secure the position

text.zh: 汉密尔顿率队攻下十号堡垒，法军攻下相邻的九号堡垒。围城继续收紧。
text.en: Hamilton's troops took Redoubt No. 10, while French forces took the neighboring Redoubt No. 9. The siege tightened.

text.zh: 数日后，英军在约克镇投降。胜利来自许多人的共同作战。战争尚未正式结束，但局势已经改变。
text.en: Days later, British forces surrendered at Yorktown. Victory belonged to many people fighting together. The war had not formally ended, but its course had changed.

text.zh: 那些从前只能写进信里的愿望，现在终于有了重量。明天，还会有人问，我们准备拿这个胜利做什么。
text.en: The hopes I once could only put in letters finally have weight. Tomorrow, someone will ask what we intend to do with this victory.
